ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening at onboarding and on an event-driven continuous basis of every general partner, limited partner, and ultimate beneficial owner against: (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (Council Regulations 269/2014, 881/2002 and related regimes), (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List, (iii) the OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists where a US nexus exists, and (iv) Luxembourg domestic designations published by the Ministry of Finance. PEP identification must be made against recognized commercial databases with enhanced due diligence, including source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation, for any person holding a prominent public function; adverse media checks are mandatory. All screening must be documented and retained for five years following termination of the business relationship, in accordance with the amended Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02, and subject to CSSF/FIU supervisory review.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), accessed through the guichet.lu e-platform and RESA electronic filing portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory name must be written in the Latin alphabet; French, German, and Luxembourgish designations are acceptable. The legal-form suffix 'SCSp' or 'Société en commandite spéciale' must appear as the final element. The name must be distinctive within the RCS and must not be identical or confusingly similar to a pre-existing RCS-registered name, a Luxembourg or Community trademark, or a name reserved by a third party. Names in non-Latin scripts require a verified transliteration into the Latin alphabet and may include a secondary non-Latin name, provided the Latin version remains the sole statutory name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANK / BANQUE / CAISSE (prior CSSF authorization required)
ASSURANCE / INSURANCE / RÉASSURANCE (prior Commissariat aux Assurances authorization required)
BOURSE / STOCK EXCHANGE / MARCHÉ RÉGLEMENTÉ (reserved to regulated market operators)
CHAMBRE / CHAMBER / ORDRE (misleading connotation of a public or professional body)
CROIX-ROUGE / RED CROSS / INTERNATIONAL MONETARY FUND (reserved to recognized institutions)
ÉTAT / STATE / GOUVERNEMENT / ADMINISTRATION (misleading use of public authority)
SICAV / SICAF / FCP / SIF / RAIF (reserved to regulated collective investment vehicles)
FIDUCIARY / TRUST / FIDUCIAIRE (subject to CSSF licensing or prior ministerial authorization)
LUXEMBOURG / NATIONAL / GRAND-DUCHAL (accepted only with a genuine local nexus and justified business purpose)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon formal rejection by the RCS registrar, the applicant must, within 15 business days, resubmit a corrected or alternative name through the RESA portal. If the corrected submission is again refused, written appeal must be lodged within two months of notification before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'Arrondissement de Luxembourg), Commercial Chamber, attaching the registrar's refusal, prior-art and trademark search evidence, and a legal memorandum on distinctiveness. The court renders its decision within approximately six weeks; an adverse first-instance judgment may be appealed to the Court of Appeal of Luxembourg within 40 days. The reservation window may be renewed once upon payment of the applicable renewal tariff.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible only with a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent. The SCSp must maintain a real, physically identifiable registered office in Luxembourg where central administration is effectively located. A purely virtual address is not acceptable for ISIC 3250/NAICS 334510 medical-device assembly and calibration operations, as the activity requires a physical base, calibrated equipment, and qualified personnel. The use of a registered-office service must be supported by genuine substance (board decisions, corporate records, personnel or outsourced management) to avoid re-characterization under Article 168 bis of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (CFC rules), BEPS Action 5 substance requirements, and the general anti-abuse rule of Article 6 AGO.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Elevated: approximately 35–45% annual probability of unannounced on-site inspection by the Luxembourg Ministry of Health (Direction de la Santé) and notified bodies for medical-device regulatory compliance and CE-marking audits; approximately 10–15% frequency of substance audits by the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (Administration des Contributions Directes) within the first three fiscal years; the CSSF and the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) conduct primarily off-site AML/CFT documentary inspections.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (SCSp provisions: Articles 102-116, introduced by the Law of 23 June 2016); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Business Registers, RCS registration and publications, as amended; Law of 27 July 1998 on electronic exchange of data and filing via eJustice.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS), Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (SCSp partnership agreement / contrat de societe) executed as a private deed or notarial act and filed electronically through the eJustice / Guichet.lu portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital and no mandatory paid-up capital for the SCSp; capital commitments are freely contractually set; no escrow or capital-blocking bank certificate is required by the RCS for registration. Cash and in-kind contributions are permitted; in-kind contributions need no statutory auditor valuation unless the partners require it. Transparent or AIF-regulated structures may impose extra capitalization by contract.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned, being the sole general partner and acting as prospective gerant, hereby resolves: (1) the partnership agreement of [●] SCSp, including the subscription lists and capital commitments, is approved and adopted; (2) the registered office is fixed at 14, rue du Fosse, L-1536 Luxembourg; (3) M. [●] is appointed gerant with full power to manage, represent and bind the SCSp, including opening bank accounts, signing electronic filings and instructing Luxembourg counsel; (4) the gerant is authorised to complete RCS registration, RESA publication, tax, VAT and social security filings, and all licence applications concerning assembly and calibration of electronic patient monitors; (5) all preparatory acts are ratified. This resolution is immediate and binding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name availability check and non-confusion certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS via eJustice portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an online name inquiry through the RCS/eJustice counter. Obtain the 'certificat de non-confusion' (non-confusion certificate) confirming that the proposed name of the SCSp, [●] SCSp, does not collide with an existing registered name and that the suffix 'Societe en Commandite Speciale' or 'SCSp' is included. Submit the name list and identification of the partners together with the application; the certificate is preliminary and does not guarantee final approval.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and suffix
Passport copies of the general and limited partners
Certificate of good standing / board resolution of corporate general partner (if any)
Power of attorney granted to Luxembourg counsel
AML/KYC identification form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS refuses the name on confusion grounds, file an amended name or appeal the RCS decision before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg within 15 days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (if notarial form chosen) or all partners in private deed; final submission sits with the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement containing the firm name, registered office, corporate object (multi-parameter bedside telemetry monitor assembly and calibration), duration, management and control rights, capital commitments, profit-sharing, transfer of interests and dissolution terms. Execute the deed by authenticated notarial act or by private electronic signature compliant with eIDAS. Ensure the deed records any appointment of the gerant and the designated registered office address.
required_dossiers: Final draft partnership agreement
Passports / national IDs of all partners
Proof of residential address for each partner
Beneficial ownership (UBO) information
Corporate resolutions of any body-corporate general partner
Certificate of non-confusion
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or counsel raises incompleteness, amend the draft by a deed of rectification or a supplemental private deed and obtain new signatures; electronic signatures secure immediate remedy before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS, registration division, via eJustice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed constitutive act and the standard registration application through the eJustice portal. Attach identity details of the gerant, the UBO declaration, the registered office address and the signed consent of the gerant. The RCS verifies legality, assigns the RCS registration number and publishes the required particulars in the Recueil electronique des societes et associations (RESA). Download the final RCS extract for onward filings.
required_dossiers: Signed partnership agreement (certified scan or notarial minute)
Application form for RCS registration
Statement of acceptance by the gerant
UBO declaration
Power of attorney and legalisation evidence
Certificate of non-confusion
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to RCS queries within the given eJustice deadline with supplementary particulars or corrected deeds; if registration is refused, appeal to the Tribunal d'arrondissement (commercial chamber) under the Law of 19 December 2002.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account opening and funding of capital commitments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg licensed credit institution (bank) and CSSF-licensed professional corporate services provider for KYC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a segregated partnership account in the name of the SCSp at a Luxembourg bank. Present the preliminary or final RCS extract, the partnership agreement, UBO declarations and source-of-funds documents for each partner. Fund the registered capital commitments by SWIFT LC or TT wire transfers from partners' bank accounts; no notarial proof of deposit is required for the SCSp, but the bank will confirm receipt of funds as part of its own KYC and account-activation routine.
required_dossiers: RCS extract or eJustice filing receipt
Certified copy of the partnership agreement
Passports and source-of-wealth statements of partners
UBO and AML forms of the bank
Description of the medical device activity
Pro forma invoice or business plan for telemetry monitor line
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues a KYC query, file supplementary source-of-wealth data or a legal opinion from Luxembourg counsel; if refused, escalate to the bank's compliance committee or open the account with another licensed Luxembourg institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA; Centre Commun de la Securite Sociale; customs for EORI
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the national business number (matricule) through Guichet.lu and register the SCSp in the ACD tax file. Register for VAT (TVA) because the assembly and sale of patient monitors is a taxable supply in Luxembourg. If the partnership will employ staff, register as employer with the Centre Commun de la Securite Sociale (CCSS). Apply separately for an EORI number if EEA-external components are imported.
required_dossiers: Final RCS extract
Certified copy of the partnership agreement
List of partners with residency and VAT status
Description of taxable activities and invoicing plan
Bank statement evidencing the account in the SCSp name
EORI application for customs registration (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File supplementary declarations within the ACD/AED grace periods; in case of late registration, submit a reasoned demerit request and, where a penalty has been raised, petition the competent tax office for a remission or ask a Luxembourg tax adviser to challenge it within the statutory objection window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministere de l'Economie - Direction generale des classes moyennes (Ministry of the Economy, SME Licence Department) acting with Guichet.lu, together with the Direction de la Sante / Ministere de la Sante for medical device manufacturer registration under Regulation (EU) 2017/745.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'etablissement (Business Establishment Permit) under the amended Law of 30 May 2005, plus manufacturer registration for medical devices in EUDAMED and the Luxembourg competent authority register.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 (EIA screening) for assembly plants reaching the industrial thresholds under the amended Law of 10 June 1999 on classified establishments; small-scale clean-room assembly and calibration is treated as a simplified registration/declaration, and a full EIA is not mandatory for this low-impact electronic assembly activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged into the public sewer must respect the Grand-Ducal Regulation limit values (pH 6.5-9.5; BOD5 <= 500 mg/L; COD <= 1000 mg/L; total suspended solids <= 600 mg/L; heavy metals under the schedule). VOC-bearing fluxes and soldering exhausts must respect the generic emission limits of Directive 2010/75/EU, particularly total organic carbon <= 20 mg/Nm3 for waste gases when thresholds apply. All WEEE scrap must be stored separately, tracked and transferred to an authorised waste manager under the national WEEE regime.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: obtain the municipal commission de securite approval on the basis of a CGDIS (Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps) review covering means of escape, extinguishers, electrical installations and alarm systems. Structural load inspections: certificate by a Luxembourg approved engineer confirming floor and rack loads for equipment and calibration benches. Workplace clearance: health and safety inspection by the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) validating ventilation of soldering zones, ESD protection, ergonomic workstations, emergency procedures and the internal OHS policy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; single electronic portal: MyGuichet.lu / Guichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The SCSp must first obtain a Luxembourg national identification number through registration with the Luxembourg Business Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS). After RCS registration, the SCSp or its duly authorised tax representative submits the VAT registration dossier to the AEDT via MyGuichet.lu, providing constitutive documents, RCS extract, description of economic activities, anticipated turnover, and a Luxembourg bank confirmation; the AEDT issues the Luxembourg TVA identification number immediately or within the standard 15-day processing window.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no domestic check-the-box election; the SCSp is fiscally transparent by default. Available statutory elections include: (i) option to be part of a VAT group as an assujetti unique under Article 62 of the Luxembourg VAT law; (ii) option for the VAT small business exemption under Article 57 if annual taxable turnover is below EUR 35,000 (input VAT recovery foregone); (iii) election for the EU One-Stop Shop (OSS) scheme for intra-EU distance sales; (iv) election under double tax treaties and domestic ATAD rules for the tax treatment of hybrid entities to be aligned with partner jurisdictions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA) / VAT
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic Luxembourg-established taxable persons have no general registration threshold; registration is mandatory from the first taxable transaction, except for the optional small business exemption up to EUR 35,000 annual turnover. Non-resident suppliers with no Luxembourg establishment are required to register from their first taxable supply in Luxembourg. For intra-EU distance sales by an EU-established supplier, the annual cross-border threshold is EUR 10,000, beyond which VAT registration or OSS usage in Luxembourg becomes mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory continuous transaction control system. E-invoicing is permitted provided the authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and legibility are ensured. B2B e-invoicing may be used by mutual consent; all VAT returns and recapitulative statements are filed electronically through MyGuichet.lu. No fiscal clearance API or government-side real-time validation of individual invoices is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods exported from Luxembourg to a destination outside the European Union qualify for the 0% VAT rate when the exporter retains evidence that the goods physically left the EU within the statutory export window and that the export is supported by customs documentation. Also eligible for 0% are certain services directly related to the exportation of goods (e.g., loading, handling, transport and customs brokerage) and intra-Community supplies to a VAT-registered EU customer where the customer's VAT identification number and EC Sales List requirements are satisfied. The SCSp must be the exporter according to the customs declaration and hold original transport documentation evidencing exit from the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document – SAD / DMS Export Declaration with exit confirmation)
Bill of Lading (For sea carriage), Air Waybill (For air cargo) or CMR road consignment note
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 evidence of payment receipt in the exporting entity's bank account
Transport contract or freight forwarding instructions
Proof of delivery to the non-EU customer or to the customer's appointed forwarder
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Luxembourg AEDT rigorously audits export zero-rating claims. If the export proof is incomplete, forged, or the goods are returned to Luxembourg or diverted for domestic use, the VAT initially zero-rated becomes immediately payable at the standard 17% rate. Administrative late-payment interest of 0.6% per month accrues from the date the VAT would originally have fallen due. Fines of up to 50% of the evaded tax may be imposed for negligence or misstatement; deliberate VAT evasion or falsification of export documentation carrying criminal liability may result in fines up to EUR 250,000 and custodial sanctions. Persons involved in abusive circular export schemes are jointly and severally liable for the VAT clawed back.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) / Central Bank of Luxembourg, acting in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking conduct, AML/CFT supervision, and payment system oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a fully integrated eurozone jurisdiction with unrestricted capital and current account convertibility for legal entities and partnerships. The euro is freely convertible, and there are no exchange-control restrictions on the import or export of capital, dividend remittance, profit distribution, or liquidation proceeds. Capital movements to and from non-EU states are governed by EU free-movement-of-capital principles and subject only to standard financial sanctions screening, AML/KYC checks, and statistical balance-of-payments reporting to the BCL. Profit remittances from a Luxembourg SCSp to partners are not subject to FX approval or currency conversion mandates; however, tax-related considerations such as domestic anti-abuse rules and possible withholding obligations on certain passive income streams remain independently applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to repatriate export receipts within a prescribed period. Export proceeds and any foreign-currency holdings may be retained on account, converted at commercial market rates, or used directly for offshore or onshore disbursements, subject only to internal bank compliance and EU sanctions regulations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium with strong legal constraints. Luxembourg-authorised and EEA-passported electronic money institutions and payment institutions may be used for low-value operational collections, FX conversion, and SEPA/wire transfers. However, digital EMIs generally do not support full trade-finance products (including standby and commercial letters of credit), high-limit escrow facilities, or nuanced multi-currency treasury structures. The Luxembourg SCSp must maintain at least one relationship with a fully licensed credit institution or a large internationally active bank to access robust SWIFT MT103 clearing, LC confirmation, and cross-currency hedging. EMIs cannot provide credit, are not eligible for client-money safeguarding equivalent to a banking licence, and are often subject to stricter sub-limit transaction thresholds. Legal constraints under the EU Payment Services Directive 2 and Luxembourg law of 10 November 2009 require EMI accounts to be opened in the name of the SCSp with full beneficial-owner transparency and seamless AML/KYC integration.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg credit institutions generally require a physical meeting with at least one authorised representative (a general partner or a designated senior manager) before opening accounts for non-resident SCSp structures. Remote onboarding is increasingly possible for low-risk, transparent structures, particularly when the SCSp has a Luxembourg registered office and a Luxembourg-resident authorised manager; however, banks retain full discretion under CSSF AML/CFT circulars to require in-person interviews at the time of KYC review. A hybrid posture is recommended: complete a physical or virtual documentary due-diligence session first, remain open to an on-site interview at the bank's Luxembourg premises, and provide the account mandate in original notarised or apostilled form where the SCSp's partnership agreement stipulates multiple signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex ownership of the SCSp with multiple non-EU limited partners and an unregulated general partner, causing ambiguity as to the identity of the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the duly executed and notarised partnership agreement (contrat de société), the Luxembourg RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) extract or relevant UBO declaration proving individual ownership above the statutory threshold, organisational chart with full legal-entity breakdown, passports of all UBOs, and a written legal opinion from a Luxembourg attorney confirming the SCSp's pass-through characteristics and the absence of disguised trusteeship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of initial capital injection and subsequent trade-related payment flows not clearly correlated to the stated medical-device business model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide audited or certified financial statements or pro-forma capital source statements, signed capital subscription agreements, bank reference letters from the transferring bank, commercial invoices and purchase orders from the target buyers of the bedside telemetry monitors, certificates of origin or CE marking documentation supporting the legitimacy of the equipment, and a detailed treasury projection matching payment rails to the corporate transaction lifecycle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) configuration triggered by any partner, director, intermediary, or counterparty in the distribution chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide fully completed sanctions-screening questionnaires for every UBO, director, general partner, and commercial counterparty; redacted yet traceable order contracts demonstrating end-use rather than strategic or military applications; certifications of non-engagement with restricted jurisdictions; and a remediation letter from the general partner accepting full responsibility for post-onboarding sanctions compliance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of higher-risk invoicing from offshore trade intermediaries or reliance on back-to-back documentary credits that obscure the commercial substance of the electronic patient monitor manufacturing chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide direct manufacturer quotations, logistics contracts, full-chain purchase orders from the OEM or component suppliers, packing lists, airway or bill-of-lading templates, customs and tariff classification documentation for ISIC 3250 / NAICS 334510, and a finalised trade-flow diagram showing the SCSp as the principal principal rather than a pass-through intermediary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential classification of the SCSp as a net taxable intermediary outside Luxembourg due to cross-border trade in physical goods, triggering substance and BEPS scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide economic-substance documentation including the Luxembourg registered address and lease agreement, minutes of partner meetings held in Luxembourg, resumés of Luxembourg-resident officers, employment contracts of qualifying local managers, an annual transfer-pricing file, and a board-approved business plan demonstrating real Luxembourg decision-making for procurement, treasury, and distribution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use standard SWIFT MT103 wire transfers from the investors' bank account to the SCSp's Luxembourg operational account with ISO 20022 remittance code 'S303' (equity financing) or 'P012' (other investment) where permitted by the sending institution. The injection must be supported by a capital subscription agreement, a call notice issued by the general partner, an updated register of partners, and a certificate from the BCL for balance-of-payments statistical reporting when the payment equals or exceeds the BCL's reporting threshold. For additional regulatory compliance, mark the field 'Purpose of Payment' with unambiguously clear wording such as 'SCSP Capital Contribution – Limited Partnership Equity – Medical Device Hardware Development and Manufacturing'. All payments should be subject to pre-screening against EU sanctions and verified against the bank's KYC redemption and source-of-funds assessment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For component sourcing and trade settlements, the primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 creditor payments for para-trade disbursements and documentary commercial letters of credit (L/C) for larger, delivery-risk-managed purchases. The SCSp may instruct the Luxembourg issuing bank to open an irrevocable, confirmation-eligible L/C in favour of the supplier, with payment conditioned upon presentation of compliant shipping and inspection documents such as original bills of lading/airway bills, commercial invoices, packing lists, certificates of origin, CE conformity certificates, and insured cargo documentation. Settlement clearing occurs TARGET2 for eurozone transactions and via correspondent banks through the broader SWIFT network for USD, CNY, and other foreign-currency obligations. Intra-group treasury sweeps may additionally use SWIFT gpi or automated concentration accounts to centralise liquidity into the primary Luxembourg treasury hub.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: AUD/USD and EUR/USD outright FX forwards (plain vanilla) traded under an ISDA or local EMTA FX master agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or less-liquid south-east Asian or Middle Eastern currencies where physical settlement is prohibited
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD or EUR/CNY) for long-term matching of mismatched procurement liabilities and customer receivables
European-style FX options with a premium paid up-front for asymmetric hedge protection on large patient-monitor export contracts
FX rollovers and tom-next swaps for managing short-term working-capital positions in the treasury account

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate effective headline rate in Luxembourg City (17% corporate income tax above EUR 175,000, plus 7% solidarity surcharge and 6.75% municipal business tax; 15% on the first EUR 175,000). The Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) is fiscally transparent, so the rate is assessed at the partner level on allocated profit, not at the SCSp level.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday; principal reliefs: 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (10% shareholding or EUR 6 million acquisition cost, 12-month holding); 80% IP-box exemption, Nexus-compliant, reducing the effective rate on qualifying IP income to approximately 4.99%; investment tax credit for digital and equity-eligible investment; R&D super-deduction; transparent SCSp allocations preserve the character of income for treaty and consolidation purposes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 887 (corporate income tax return) filed electronically via the eCDF platform of the Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) and the MyGuichet.lu portal; for the SCSp, a partnership transparency annex must accompany the return identifying each partner, profit-share percentage and allocable taxable income.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return for a fiscal year closing on 31 December must be filed by 31 December of the following calendar year; for non-calendar fiscal years, the deadline is 31 December of the year following the accounting close. Extensions must be requested before the statutory deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RCS registration number, legal form code (SCSp), ISIC/NACE industrial classification, share capital, and tax identification numbers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the non-resident partner's name, registered address, country of residence and confirm whether a Luxembourg permanent establishment (PE) exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the accounting period covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-calendar fiscal years are recognised if the accounts are closed consistently and the RCS approval is attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit or loss of the SCSp, followed by the allocation of that result to each partner according to the partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only profit attributable to a Luxembourg PE of the non-resident partner is declared in Luxembourg; other allocations are reported in the partner's state of residence and protected under the applicable DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible items: fines, non-deductible entertainment expenses, 50% of business-meal expenses, certain taxes, and excessive remuneration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The add-back is allocated to partners per the profit-sharing ratio; the non-resident's treaty relief is unaffected by such add-backs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of qualifying dividend income and capital gains from the taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An EU or treaty-resident corporate partner with a qualifying holding (10% or EUR 6 million acquisition cost, 12-month holding period) must attach the holding certificate and TRC to substantiate the exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule C.2 - IP and R&D Claims
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the Nexus-ratio-exempt profit for qualifying intellectual property and the R&D/investment tax credit claim.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The claim is allowed only if the partner is the legal and economic owner of the qualifying IP; claims cascading to zero-tax jurisdictions are rejected absent economic substance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an administrative fine of up to EUR 6,000 under LIR Section 177; total omission of the return permits ex officio assessment with a 10% surcharge on the additionally assessed tax; unpaid assessed tax accrues monthly arrears interest at 0.6% per month (2024 rate); wilful false declaration attracts criminal sanctions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory Luxembourg withholding tax on dividend distributions (LIR Section 148); full relief applies to qualifying EU parent-subsidiary distributions and to non-EU shareholders under the 10%/12-month participation rule; distributions of profit allocations by a transparent SCSp are not subject to Luxembourg dividend withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must deliver a current Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) and a beneficial-ownership declaration to the Luxembourg withholding agent; where the reduced treaty rate is applied at source, no refund is needed; if full WHT was wrongly withheld, a refund is claimed through Form 105 R within the statutory limitation period (5 years). SCSp allocations do not generate a WHT event; treaty protection is asserted via the partner's residence return.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law imposes no withholding tax on interest or royalties paid to non-residents (0% statutory WHT); the EU Interest and Royalty Directive (2003/49/EC, transposed by the Law of 13 May 2008) confirms the nil rate for EU related companies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Master File and Local File apply when the multinational group's consolidated annual revenue exceeds EUR 750 million and the Luxembourg entity executes cross-border controlled transactions; a simplified Local File is required where annual intercompany transactions exceed EUR 1 million. The SCSp must document the arm's-length allocation of ECG-device assembly and calibration margins to the resident partner.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: ESR applicability: no dedicated Economic Substance Regulations of the offshore-centre type exist in Luxembourg; substance requirements are enforced through the GAAR (LIR Section 6), the ATAD anti-abuse rule (Law of 20 July 2020) and the MLI Principal Purpose Test. For a transparent SCSp, the ACD requires a real registered office, local bookkeeping, board/managerial decision-taking in Luxembourg, a Luxembourg bank account and adequate staff; absence of these factors triggers recharacterisation as opaque, denial of treaty benefits and application of the full 24.94% aggregate rate.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting scaffolded profit allocations of the SCSp from Form 887, falsifying the partnership books, or engineering artificial losses allocated to a shell partner to eliminate Luxembourg taxable base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine of up to EUR 6,000 (LIR Section 177); where fraud is established, criminal conviction under the Luxembourg Criminal Code carries a fine of up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years; ex officio reassessment plus 10% understatement surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SCSp's general partner and its directors are jointly and severally liable for unpaid partnership taxes; courts may pierce the corporate veil to recover the Treasury claim from personal assets, impose travel bans, and order civil restitution.
